evidence_rows.fact: Dell disclosed FY26 AI-optimized server orders above $64B, shipments above $25B, and FY27 starting backlog of about $43B.
evidence_rows.supports: AI server revenue demand is real and issuer-disclosed.
evidence_rows.cannot_infer: Does not prove AI server gross margin, GPU pass-through cost, customer concentration, or per-customer order size.

evidence_rows.fact: Dell disclosed ISG revenue, Servers and Networking revenue, Storage revenue, and ISG operating income / margin.
evidence_rows.supports: ISG is the financial bridge through which AI server orders should show revenue and margin quality.
evidence_rows.cannot_infer: Does not split AI server gross margin, Blackwell mix, attach rate, or customer-level profitability.

evidence_rows.fact: Dell official announcements connect PowerEdge XE9680 to H200/B200 and XE9712 to the GB200 NVL72 platform.
evidence_rows.supports: Dell has a concrete NVIDIA-powered AI server / rack product path.
evidence_rows.cannot_infer: Does not prove revenue, order volume, signed customer contracts, or gross margin.

evidence_rows.fact: Dell's XE9712 / Integrated Rack path links GB200 NVL72 to a concrete OEM rack-scale AI server configuration.
evidence_rows.supports: Product analysis can connect NVIDIA rack-scale architecture to Dell's server product surface.
evidence_rows.cannot_infer: Does not prove Dell revenue, customer order value, shipment count, or system gross margin.

evidence_rows.fact: GB200 NVL72 is a rack-scale system with 36 Grace CPUs, 72 Blackwell GPUs, a large NVLink domain, and liquid-cooled deployment.
evidence_rows.supports: NVIDIA product advantage is system-level, not just single-GPU compute.
evidence_rows.cannot_infer: Does not prove SKU revenue, Dell orders, customer purchase volume, ASP, or margin.

evidence_rows.fact: NVIDIA disclosed record revenue and high Data Center revenue growth.
evidence_rows.supports: AI accelerator demand has entered NVIDIA financials, not just macro narrative.
evidence_rows.cannot_infer: Does not split B200/GB200/GB300 SKU revenue or Dell share.

evidence_rows.fact: AMD MI300X discloses 192GB HBM3 memory, 5.3 TB/s bandwidth, CDNA3, FP8 and FP16 support.
evidence_rows.supports: AMD is a real accelerator substitute in memory-heavy inference/training workloads.
evidence_rows.cannot_infer: Does not prove market share, customer migration scale, or NVIDIA pricing pressure by itself.

evidence_rows.fact: AMD reported MI355X MLPerf inference progress and MLCommons provides the public benchmark framework for cross-system comparison.
evidence_rows.supports: AMD competitive capability and software stack progress are real product-performance signals.
evidence_rows.cannot_infer: Benchmark does not directly prove procurement, revenue, share, ASP, or gross margin.

evidence_rows.fact: Google Cloud TPU docs disclose TPU compute, HBM, ICI, pod size, and network/all-reduce characteristics.
evidence_rows.supports: TPU is a real hyperscaler custom-silicon alternative to external GPUs in selected workloads.
evidence_rows.cannot_infer: Does not prove replacement ratio, internal procurement cadence, or NVIDIA revenue loss.

evidence_rows.fact: Google Cloud A4X preview uses GB200 NVL72 and positions B200/A4 plus GB200/A4X cloud offerings.
evidence_rows.supports: GB200 has entered a hyperscaler cloud product surface; clouds may use both NVIDIA GPUs and TPU.
evidence_rows.cannot_infer: Does not prove purchase amount, supplier revenue, availability scale, or regional capacity.

evidence_rows.fact: Microsoft disclosed large AI/cloud capex, cloud/AI revenue growth, and demand exceeding supply.
evidence_rows.supports: Hyperscaler demand pool is real and supply constrained.
evidence_rows.cannot_infer: Does not identify how much flows to NVIDIA, Dell, ODMs, networking, power/cooling, or custom silicon.

evidence_rows.fact: Amazon disclosed AWS sales and operating income growth.
evidence_rows.supports: AWS cloud demand context is positive for AI infrastructure demand pool.
evidence_rows.cannot_infer: Does not reveal AWS GPU vendor mix, Dell server purchases, or capex allocation.

evidence_rows.fact: Alphabet disclosed capex mainly for technical infrastructure, with servers/data-center network as a major share, plus Google Cloud revenue growth.
evidence_rows.supports: Google capex connects to accelerator/server demand background.
evidence_rows.cannot_infer: Does not split NVIDIA GPU versus TPU procurement.

evidence_rows.fact: Meta raised 2026 capex guidance for future capacity and cited component pricing.
evidence_rows.supports: AI demand pool and component price pressure are both active.
evidence_rows.cannot_infer: Does not prove supplier revenue or exact vendor allocation.

evidence_rows.fact: TSMC disclosed revenue, margin, advanced technology wafer revenue share, and leading-edge process demand.
evidence_rows.supports: AI/HPC demand is visible at the leading-edge foundry layer.
evidence_rows.cannot_infer: Does not disclose customer-level allocation across NVIDIA, AMD, Google, Apple, or others.

evidence_rows.fact: ASML disclosed net sales, gross margin, installed-base management, new/used lithography systems sold, and 2026 guide.
evidence_rows.supports: ASML read-through should be separated into EUV/DUV, installed base, China/export, and bookings/backlog cycle.
evidence_rows.cannot_infer: Does not prove AI-specific ASML orders or customer allocation.

evidence_rows.fact: Applied Materials disclosed revenue, gross margin, Semiconductor Systems segment, and foundry/logic/DRAM/flash mix.
evidence_rows.supports: AMAT AI read-through runs through materials engineering, deposition, foundry/logic, DRAM, flash, and advanced packaging exposure.
evidence_rows.cannot_infer: Does not replace customer order backlog or AI-specific bookings.

evidence_rows.fact: Lam Research disclosed revenue, gross margin, operating margin, and AI-driven demand management commentary.
evidence_rows.supports: LRCX read-through should focus on etch/deposition, memory/HBM, advanced packaging, and process intensity.
evidence_rows.cannot_infer: Does not prove each HBM or advanced packaging customer order.

evidence_rows.fact: The current business evidence pack does not include valuation percentiles, ownership/positioning, options/short interest, ETF flows, or event reaction asymmetry.
evidence_rows.supports: The workpaper can say business evidence is directionally positive but cannot issue a price-sensitive recommendation without capital-feedback data.
evidence_rows.cannot_infer: Cannot infer price-in, crowding, upside/downside skew, or trading recommendation.

evidence_rows.fact: The core counter-thesis includes capex digestion, OEM margin dilution, AMD/TPU substitution, HBM/CoWoS/power bottlenecks, export controls, customer concentration, and price-in risk.
evidence_rows.supports: Counter-thesis and what-would-change must be part of the main workpaper, not a generic appendix.
evidence_rows.cannot_infer: Does not quantify probability or valuation impact without follow-up data.

required_items: Whether AI server demand improves DELL quality of earnings or only adds low-margin pass-through revenue.
How NVDA/AMD/TPU product capability and supply affect server OEM and semicap read-through.
Which customer deployment or official relationship signals support adoption, and what they cannot prove.
How foundry, advanced packaging, HBM, and semicap cycles connect to the AI demand pool.
Whether market expectations and price-in risk change the interpretation of fundamentals.
pass_conditions: Memo has a clear thesis before caveats.
Memo connects product, deployment, supply chain, financial quality, market expectation, and counter-thesis.
Each required item is answered or typed as a bounded gap with root-cause category.
Cannot-infer boundaries are stated without turning the memo into a non-answer.
fail_conditions: Output says product layer cannot be judged only because SKU revenue is missing.
Output treats hyperscaler capex as direct supplier order allocation.
Output says financial data is missing when accepted upstream payload contains relevant facts.
Output is primarily a list of evidence rather than a judgment path.
